overview: Data Lineage is the end-to-end tracking of data's origin, movement, and transformations as it flows through systems — from source, through every pipeline and transformation, to its final consumption in tables, dashboards, and ML models.
It answers 'where did this data come from, what happened to it, and what depends on it', enabling impact analysis, root-cause debugging, and regulatory compliance.

Lineage exists at multiple granularities — dataset/table-level (which tables feed which) and the finer column-level (which source columns derive which target columns) — and is captured by parsing code/queries or by emitting runtime events (e.g., OpenLineage).
learningObjectives: Understand what data lineage is and the questions it answers (provenance, impact, root cause, compliance).
Distinguish table-level from column-level lineage and know when each is needed.
Learn how lineage is captured (SQL parsing vs runtime event emission) and modeled as a directed acyclic graph.
Implement and reason about lineage using OpenLineage, Marquez, and platform-native lineage (e.g., Unity Catalog).
coreConcept.formalDefinition: Data Lineage is the documented, queryable representation — typically a directed acyclic graph of datasets and the jobs/transformations that connect them — of the complete lifecycle of data: its sources (provenance), every movement and transformation it undergoes, and all downstream artifacts that consume it, captured at dataset (table) and/or attribute (column) granularity.
coreConcept.simpleExplanation: Imagine a family tree, but for data. For any number on a dashboard, lineage lets you trace its 'ancestors' — the exact source tables and columns and the transformations that produced it — and its 'descendants' — every report or model that would be affected if that data changed or broke.
coreConcept.historicalContext: Lineage began as manual ETL documentation and metadata in data warehouses and tools like Informatica. As pipelines exploded across heterogeneous tools (Airflow, Spark, dbt, Kafka), manual approaches couldn't keep up. The OpenLineage open standard (a Linux Foundation project) emerged around 2020-2021 to standardize automatic lineage capture across tools, with Marquez as its reference metadata store, and cloud catalogs like Databricks Unity Catalog and others adding automatic column-level lineage.

whyItMatters.business: Builds trust in data by making metrics traceable and auditable, accelerates root-cause analysis when reports look wrong, and is often mandatory for regulatory reporting (e.g., BCBS 239, GDPR, SOX).
whyItMatters.engineering: Enables impact analysis before changes ('what breaks if I alter this column?'), faster incident debugging by tracing failures to their source, and safer refactoring of pipelines.
whyItMatters.scalability: In large organizations with thousands of datasets and pipelines, automated lineage is the only feasible way to understand dependencies and avoid hidden breakages.
whyItMatters.cost: Reduces the cost of incidents (faster root cause), prevents costly broken-downstream changes, and identifies unused/orphaned datasets that can be deprecated.
whyItMatters.reliability: Provides the dependency map needed for data observability and SLAs, so teams know what is affected when a source is late, schema-changed, or corrupted.

coreComponents.name: Lineage Graph (Datasets + Jobs)
coreComponents.definition: A directed acyclic graph where nodes are datasets (and optionally columns) and edges are the jobs/transformations that read inputs and produce outputs.
coreComponents.purpose: Provide a queryable model to traverse upstream (provenance) and downstream (impact) from any node.
coreComponents.responsibilities: Represent producer-consumer relationships, support graph traversal, and store run-level history.

coreComponents.name: Lineage Capture Mechanism
coreComponents.definition: The means of extracting lineage: parsing SQL/transformation code statically, or emitting runtime events from jobs as they execute.
coreComponents.purpose: Populate the lineage graph automatically and keep it in sync with what actually runs.
coreComponents.responsibilities: Detect inputs/outputs (and column derivations), handle many engines, and attach run metadata.
coreComponents.examples: OpenLineage integration in Airflow/Spark/dbt emitting START/COMPLETE run events with input/output datasets and column facets.

coreComponents.name: Metadata Store / Catalog
coreComponents.definition: A backend that persists lineage and metadata and exposes APIs/UI for querying it (e.g., Marquez, DataHub, Unity Catalog, OpenMetadata, Atlas).
coreComponents.purpose: Store, index, and serve lineage for browsing, impact analysis, and governance.
coreComponents.responsibilities: Persist graph + versions, expose search/traversal APIs, integrate access control and documentation.
coreComponents.examples: Marquez storing OpenLineage events; Unity Catalog auto-capturing table and column lineage for Databricks.

coreComponents.name: Column-Level Resolver
coreComponents.definition: The component that maps which source columns contribute to each target column by analyzing transformation expressions.
coreComponents.purpose: Provide fine-grained lineage for precise impact analysis and compliance (e.g., tracing PII).
coreComponents.responsibilities: Parse SELECT expressions, joins, and functions to attribute each output column to its input columns.
coreComponents.examples: Resolving that gold.daily_revenue.total_revenue derives from silver.orders.amount via SUM.

internalWorking: When a pipeline runs, the capture mechanism identifies the job's input datasets and output datasets — by parsing the SQL/query plan or by an integration emitting structured events.
For column-level lineage, the transformation's logical plan or parsed SQL is analyzed to attribute each output column to the specific input columns (and functions) that produced it.

These inputs, outputs, and column mappings are emitted as lineage events (e.g., OpenLineage RunEvents with START/RUNNING/COMPLETE/FAIL states) carrying a run id, job name, datasets, schema facets, and column-lineage facets.
A metadata store ingests the events and materializes/updates the lineage DAG, versioning datasets and recording each run so historical lineage and freshness can be queried.

Users (or automated tools) then traverse the graph: upstream to find provenance/root cause, downstream to perform impact analysis, and across runs to audit how a value was produced at a point in time.
coreConcept.architectureFlow: Pipelines/Jobs (Airflow, Spark, dbt, SQL engines) -> Lineage Capture (SQL parse or OpenLineage emission) -> Lineage Events (inputs/outputs + schema + column facets) -> Metadata Store/Catalog (Marquez, Unity Catalog, DataHub) -> Lineage Graph -> UI/APIs for impact analysis, root cause, compliance.
dataFlowWalkthrough: 1. A dbt model 'daily_revenue' runs, selecting SUM(amount) from silver.orders joined to silver.customers.

2. The OpenLineage dbt integration parses the compiled SQL and emits a run event: inputs [silver.orders, silver.customers], output [gold.daily_revenue], plus a column-lineage facet mapping total_revenue <- silver.orders.amount.
3. Marquez ingests the event and updates the lineage DAG, versioning gold.daily_revenue and recording the run with timing.
4. Later, a dashboard shows wrong revenue; an engineer queries lineage upstream from gold.daily_revenue and finds the run, the input tables, and the column derivation.
5. They also run downstream impact analysis from silver.orders before altering its 'amount' column, discovering every report/model that would be affected.

keyTerminology.meaning: The origin and transformation history of a dataset — where its data came from and how it was produced.
keyTerminology.importance: Foundation for root-cause analysis, auditability, and trust in a value's correctness.

keyTerminology.meaning: Identifying all artifacts that depend on a dataset/column so you know what a change or failure affects.
keyTerminology.importance: Lets you safely change schemas/logic and assess blast radius of incidents before they propagate.

keyTerminology.meaning: Fine-grained lineage mapping each output column to the specific input columns (and functions) that derive it.
keyTerminology.importance: Essential for precise impact analysis and compliance (e.g., tracing where PII flows).

keyTerminology.meaning: An open standard (Linux Foundation) defining a model and API for emitting lineage events (runs, jobs, datasets, facets) across tools.
keyTerminology.importance: Standardizes automatic, tool-agnostic lineage capture so heterogeneous stacks produce interoperable lineage.

keyTerminology.meaning: An extensible piece of metadata attached to an OpenLineage run, job, or dataset (e.g., schema facet, columnLineage facet, dataQuality facet).
keyTerminology.importance: Lets lineage carry rich context (schema, column derivations, quality) without changing the core model.

importantConcepts.explanation: Static lineage is derived by parsing code/SQL without running it (e.g., dbt graph, SQL parsers), reflecting intended dependencies. Runtime lineage is emitted as jobs execute (OpenLineage), reflecting what actually happened including run timing and failures. Production observability favors runtime lineage; design-time helps pre-deploy impact analysis.

Table-level lineage shows which tables feed which (cheaper, simpler). Column-level shows which source columns derive each target column (richer, harder to compute) and is required for precise PII tracing and minimal-blast-radius change analysis.

importantConcepts.concept: Lineage as a DAG with Run History
importantConcepts.explanation: Lineage is modeled as a directed acyclic graph of datasets and jobs, but each edge is realized by runs over time, so the store keeps run history to answer 'how was this value produced on that date' and to track freshness/failures.

variationsAndTypes: **Table/Dataset-level lineage:** Tracks producer-consumer relationships between whole datasets; simplest and most common.
**Column/field-level lineage:** Maps individual column derivations; needed for precise impact and compliance.
**Job/process-level lineage:** Focuses on the jobs/transformations connecting datasets, with run metadata.
**End-to-end / cross-system lineage:** Stitches lineage across ingestion, warehouse, BI, and ML to follow data from source system to dashboard.
**Business lineage vs technical lineage:** Business lineage maps human-meaningful flows for stewards; technical lineage maps physical tables/columns/jobs for engineers.
advantages: **Impact Analysis:** Know exactly what breaks before changing a schema, column, or pipeline.
**Faster Root-Cause Debugging:** Trace a bad metric back through transformations to the source quickly.
**Compliance and Auditability:** Demonstrate data provenance and PII flow for regulations (GDPR, BCBS 239, SOX).
**Trust and Discoverability:** Lets consumers understand and trust data, and helps identify orphaned/unused datasets.
disadvantages: **Capture Complexity:** Comprehensive, accurate lineage across many heterogeneous tools is hard to build and maintain.
**Column-Level Cost:** Resolving column-level lineage requires parsing complex SQL/plans and can be incomplete for dynamic or UDF-heavy logic.
**Staleness Risk:** Static lineage can drift from reality; lineage must be kept in sync with what actually runs.
**Storage/Operational Overhead:** Capturing and storing run-level lineage at scale adds infrastructure and maintenance.

tradeOffs.whenToUse: Invest in automated lineage when you have many interdependent pipelines, regulatory/audit requirements, frequent schema changes, or recurring 'why is this number wrong' incidents — i.e., most non-trivial data platforms.
tradeOffs.whenToAvoid: Full column-level, cross-system lineage may be overkill for a tiny, single-pipeline setup where dependencies are obvious; table-level or even documentation-based lineage can suffice until complexity grows.

coreConcept.realWorldAnalogy: Data lineage is like the supply-chain traceability on food packaging. If a contamination is found in a batch of cookies (a bad metric), traceability lets you trace back through the bakery, the flour supplier, and the specific wheat farm (root cause), and trace forward to every store and shipment that received that batch (impact analysis) so you can recall exactly what's affected.

commonMisconceptions.myth: Table-level lineage is enough for everything.
commonMisconceptions.reality: Table-level shows which tables connect but not which columns derive which. For PII tracing, precise impact analysis, and minimizing change blast radius, column-level lineage is required.

commonMisconceptions.myth: Lineage is just static documentation you write once.
commonMisconceptions.reality: Useful lineage is automatically captured and kept in sync with running pipelines (runtime/OpenLineage). Hand-written docs go stale immediately in evolving systems.

commonMisconceptions.myth: Lineage and a data catalog are the same thing.
commonMisconceptions.reality: A catalog organizes and describes datasets; lineage is the dependency graph among them. Modern catalogs often include lineage, but lineage is a distinct capability (provenance/impact/root cause).

productionConsiderations.scalability: At thousands of datasets and runs/day, the metadata store must index and traverse large graphs efficiently and ingest high event volume; partition/version datasets, prune old runs, and use graph-friendly storage. Column-level resolution must be batched and incremental.
productionConsiderations.reliability: Lineage capture should be non-blocking and fault-isolated — emitting lineage must never crash or slow the actual pipeline; events are typically sent asynchronously and the store handles retries/duplicates idempotently.
productionConsiderations.faultTolerance: Use idempotent event ingestion keyed by run id so retries don't double-count; buffer/queue events so a temporarily down metadata store doesn't lose lineage; degrade gracefully to table-level if column resolution fails.
productionConsiderations.monitoring: Monitor lineage coverage (% of jobs emitting lineage), event ingestion lag, failed/incomplete runs, and column-resolution success rate; alert on coverage gaps that blind impact analysis.
productionConsiderations.security: Lineage metadata can reveal sensitive schema/PII flows; secure the catalog with access controls and audit logging, and use column-level lineage to enforce and prove PII handling.
productionConsiderations.costOptimization: Capture lineage automatically (no manual labor), retain run history with sensible TTLs, and use lineage to find and deprecate unused datasets, reducing storage/compute waste.
productionConsiderations.performance: Asynchronous, low-overhead emission keeps pipeline latency unaffected; static parsing for pre-deploy impact analysis avoids runtime cost; pre-compute/index downstream sets for fast impact queries.

codeExamples.title: Emitting an OpenLineage Run Event Manually (Python)
codeExamples.overview: Use the OpenLineage Python client to emit START and COMPLETE run events with input/output datasets, modeling a job that reads two Silver tables and writes a Gold table.
codeExamples.code:
from openlineage.client import OpenLineageClient
from openlineage.client.run import RunEvent, RunState, Run, Job, Dataset
from openlineage.client.uuid import generate_new_uuid
from datetime import datetime, timezone

client = OpenLineageClient(url="http://marquez:5000")
run = Run(runId=str(generate_new_uuid()))
job = Job(namespace="analytics", name="build_daily_revenue")

inputs = [Dataset(namespace="warehouse", name="silver.orders"),
          Dataset(namespace="warehouse", name="silver.customers")]
outputs = [Dataset(namespace="warehouse", name="gold.daily_revenue")]
now = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()

client.emit(RunEvent(eventType=RunState.START, eventTime=now,
                     run=run, job=job, inputs=inputs, outputs=outputs,
                     producer="https://github.com/acme/pipelines"))
# ... job executes ...
client.emit(RunEvent(eventType=RunState.COMPLETE, eventTime=now,
                     run=run, job=job, inputs=inputs, outputs=outputs,
                     producer="https://github.com/acme/pipelines"))
codeExamples.breakdown: A single runId ties the START and COMPLETE events together. The job is identified by namespace+name; inputs and outputs are datasets identified by namespace+name. The metadata store (Marquez at the client URL) ingests these to build/update the lineage DAG and record the run's timing and status.
codeExamples.expectedOutput: Marquez records a run of 'build_daily_revenue' with edges silver.orders -> gold.daily_revenue and silver.customers -> gold.daily_revenue, viewable as a lineage graph with run history.
codeExamples.commonIssues: Using different runIds for START/COMPLETE creates orphaned runs; mismatched dataset namespaces/names break graph stitching; emitting synchronously can add latency if not done carefully.
codeExamples.optimizationTips: Prefer built-in integrations (Airflow, Spark, dbt) over manual emission; emit asynchronously; keep dataset naming consistent (namespace + fully qualified name) so cross-job edges connect.

codeExamples.title: Querying Lineage from the Marquez API (Table-Level Impact Analysis)
codeExamples.overview: Call the Marquez lineage endpoint to fetch the graph around a dataset and identify downstream dependents before making a change.
codeExamples.code:
# Fetch lineage centered on a dataset node, 2 hops out (downstream impact)
curl -s "http://marquez:5000/api/v1/lineage?nodeId=dataset:warehouse:silver.orders&depth=2" | jq '.graph[] | {id, type, outEdges: .outEdges}'

# List jobs that read a dataset (its direct downstream consumers)
curl -s "http://marquez:5000/api/v1/namespaces/warehouse/datasets/silver.orders/versions" | jq '.versions[0].fields'
codeExamples.breakdown: The /lineage endpoint returns nodes and their out-edges around a starting nodeId. Traversing outEdges from silver.orders enumerates downstream jobs and datasets (impact analysis); traversing in-edges would give upstream provenance. depth controls how many hops to include.
codeExamples.expectedOutput: A JSON lineage subgraph showing that silver.orders feeds the 'build_daily_revenue' job, which produces gold.daily_revenue — i.e., the downstream artifacts affected by changing silver.orders.
codeExamples.commonIssues: Too-deep traversal returns huge graphs; missing lineage events leave gaps that hide real dependents; relying on table-level only when a column-level change needs finer analysis.
codeExamples.optimizationTips: Bound traversal depth, cache frequent impact queries, and combine with column-level facets when the change targets a specific column.

codeExamples.title: Column-Level Lineage from SQL (dbt / Unity Catalog Style)
codeExamples.overview: Show the SQL whose parsed expressions yield column-level lineage, and the resulting mapping a resolver (e.g., Unity Catalog or a SQL parser) produces.
codeExamples.code:
-- Transformation SQL (e.g., a dbt model)
CREATE TABLE gold.daily_revenue AS
SELECT
  c.region                          AS region,        -- <- silver.customers.region
  DATE(o.order_ts)                  AS order_date,     -- <- silver.orders.order_ts
  SUM(o.amount)                     AS total_revenue   -- <- silver.orders.amount
FROM silver.orders o
JOIN silver.customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
GROUP BY c.region, DATE(o.order_ts);

-- Resolved column-level lineage (conceptual mapping captured automatically):
--   gold.daily_revenue.region        <- silver.customers.region
--   gold.daily_revenue.order_date     <- silver.orders.order_ts        (via DATE)
--   gold.daily_revenue.total_revenue  <- silver.orders.amount          (via SUM)
codeExamples.breakdown: A column-level resolver parses each SELECT expression and attributes the output column to the input column(s) and function used. Join keys (customer_id) link the tables. Unity Catalog (or OpenLineage's columnLineage facet) captures these mappings automatically when the query runs.
codeExamples.expectedOutput: A column-level lineage record: total_revenue derives from silver.orders.amount via SUM, region from silver.customers.region, order_date from silver.orders.order_ts via DATE.
codeExamples.commonIssues: SELECT * obscures column mappings; UDFs, dynamic SQL, or complex expressions can make column resolution incomplete; CASE/aggregation chains require careful parsing.
codeExamples.optimizationTips: Avoid SELECT * in transformations so columns are explicit; prefer engines/catalogs with native column-level lineage; document derivations for logic the parser can't resolve.

endToEndExample.businessProblem: A finance team's revenue dashboard suddenly shows a 30% drop. Leadership needs to know within the hour whether the data is wrong or the business changed, and engineering must safely fix the root cause without breaking the dozens of reports and models that consume the same upstream data.
endToEndExample.inputData: A multi-tool stack: Airflow orchestrating Spark and dbt jobs that build silver.orders and silver.customers, then gold.daily_revenue, consumed by a BI dashboard and an ML churn model; OpenLineage integrations emit run events to Marquez, and Unity Catalog provides column-level lineage.
endToEndExample.architecture: Pipelines emit OpenLineage events (Airflow/Spark/dbt integrations) into Marquez, which stores the lineage DAG with run history. Unity Catalog captures table and column lineage for warehouse tables. A lineage UI/API supports upstream (provenance) and downstream (impact) traversal.
processingSteps: 1. The dashboard alert fires; an engineer opens lineage for gold.daily_revenue and traverses upstream.
2. Lineage shows gold.daily_revenue <- silver.orders (column total_revenue <- silver.orders.amount) and the runs that produced today's version.
3. Run history reveals the latest silver.orders run consumed a source file with a schema change that nulled 'amount' for one region.
4. The engineer fixes the parsing, then runs downstream impact analysis from silver.orders to enumerate every affected artifact (dashboard, churn model, other marts).
5. They reprocess silver.orders and gold.daily_revenue, notify the impacted downstream owners discovered via lineage, and verify the corrected metric.
endToEndExample.output: A traced root cause (a source schema change nulling a column), a complete list of downstream artifacts affected, a corrected metric, and an auditable record of provenance and runs for compliance.
endToEndExample.monitoring: Track lineage coverage across jobs, OpenLineage event ingestion lag, failed/incomplete runs surfaced in the lineage graph, and column-resolution success; alert when key jobs stop emitting lineage (blind spots).
endToEndExample.errorHandling: Lineage emission is asynchronous and idempotent (keyed by run id), so a transient Marquez outage queues events without breaking pipelines; if column-level resolution fails, the system degrades to table-level so impact analysis still works.
endToEndExample.finalResult: The incident is root-caused and remediated quickly, the full blast radius is known before changes, downstream owners are proactively notified, and the organization has an auditable, automatically maintained lineage graph spanning source to dashboard.

industryUseCases.problem: Regulations like BCBS 239 and SOX require demonstrable provenance of every reported figure and clear PII handling.
industryUseCases.solution: Automated table- and column-level lineage (e.g., via catalogs/Atlas/Unity Catalog) traces each regulatory metric back to authoritative sources and shows where PII flows.
industryUseCases.benefits: Audit-ready provenance, faster regulatory responses, and enforced/proven data-handling controls.

industryUseCases.problem: Thousands of interdependent datasets and pipelines make change impact and incident root-cause analysis intractable manually.
industryUseCases.solution: Centralized metadata and lineage systems capture dataset/job relationships across the stack to power impact analysis and debugging at scale.
industryUseCases.benefits: Safer schema changes, faster incident resolution, and discoverability of data dependencies.

industryUseCases.problem: Teams need to govern and trust data across medallion layers and many notebooks/jobs.
industryUseCases.solution: Unity Catalog automatically captures table- and column-level lineage for queries and jobs, visualizing flows from Bronze to Gold and into BI/ML.
industryUseCases.benefits: Automatic, low-effort lineage; precise impact analysis; governance and audit integrated with access control.

productionDeepDive.scalability: Large platforms emit millions of lineage events; the metadata store must ingest at high throughput and traverse graphs with millions of nodes/edges efficiently. Strategies: version datasets, prune/TTL old runs, index downstream sets for fast impact queries, and resolve column lineage incrementally per run rather than recomputing globally.
productionDeepDive.faultTolerance: Emission is decoupled from pipeline execution and idempotent by run id, so retries don't double-count and a store outage queues (not loses) events. Column resolution degrades gracefully to table-level on parse failure so impact analysis remains usable.
productionDeepDive.highAvailability: Run the metadata store/catalog as a redundant, highly available service with a durable backing database; buffer events (queue) so producers aren't blocked when the store is briefly unavailable.
productionDeepDive.disasterRecovery: Back up the lineage metadata store (graph + run history) and replicate cross-region; because lineage can also be re-derived by re-emitting from pipeline definitions/code, the source pipelines plus event history form a recoverable record.
productionDeepDive.performanceOptimization: Emit events asynchronously to avoid adding pipeline latency; use static SQL parsing for pre-deploy impact analysis without runtime cost; pre-compute and cache downstream/upstream closures for hot datasets; bound graph traversal depth in queries.
productionDeepDive.costOptimization: Automate capture (eliminate manual lineage labor), set retention TTLs on run history, and use lineage to identify and deprecate orphaned/unused datasets and pipelines, reclaiming storage and compute.
productionDeepDive.securityConsiderations: Lineage exposes schema and PII flow, so protect the catalog with authentication, authorization, and audit logging; leverage column-level lineage to enforce and demonstrate PII/data-handling compliance and to scope access.
productionDeepDive.monitoringAndObservability: Treat lineage coverage as an SLI: percentage of jobs emitting lineage, event ingestion lag, count of incomplete/failed runs in the graph, and column-resolution success rate; alert on coverage regressions that create impact-analysis blind spots.
productionDeepDive.dataQualityValidation: Combine lineage with data-quality facets (e.g., OpenLineage dataQuality facet, row counts, null rates) so that when a quality check fails, lineage immediately shows the upstream cause and downstream blast radius.
productionDeepDive.loggingAndAlerting: Centralize ingestion logs of the lineage store; alert on event ingestion failures, sudden drops in emitting jobs (blind spots), and failed/incomplete runs that indicate pipeline problems traceable via the graph.

recommendedPractices: **Automate Capture (Don't Hand-Maintain):** Use OpenLineage integrations or native catalog lineage so the graph stays in sync with what actually runs.
**Capture Both Table and Column Levels:** Table-level for broad dependency maps; column-level for PII tracing and precise impact analysis.
**Decouple Emission from Execution:** Emit lineage asynchronously and idempotently so it never slows or breaks pipelines.
**Run Impact Analysis Before Changes:** Query downstream lineage before altering a schema/column to know the blast radius.
engineeringStandards: Every production job must emit lineage (table-level minimum) via a standard integration; lineage coverage is tracked as an SLI.
Use consistent, fully-qualified dataset naming (namespace + database.schema.table) so cross-job edges connect.
Avoid SELECT * in transformations so column-level lineage can be resolved accurately.
designRecommendations: Adopt the OpenLineage standard for tool-agnostic, interoperable lineage across the stack.
Store lineage with run history (a DAG plus runs) so you can answer 'how was this value produced on that date'.
Integrate lineage with the data catalog and data-quality checks for unified governance and observability.
namingConventions: Identify datasets by namespace + fully qualified name (e.g., warehouse / silver.orders) consistently across all emitters.
Name jobs by domain + purpose (e.g., analytics / build_daily_revenue) and keep run ids unique per execution.
documentationStandards: Document any derivations the parser cannot resolve (UDFs, dynamic SQL) so lineage gaps are explicit.
Maintain ownership metadata on datasets so impact analysis can notify the right downstream owners.
Record which datasets contain PII and rely on column lineage to demonstrate its flow for compliance.
testingStrategies: Verify integrations emit correct inputs/outputs by asserting expected edges appear in the metadata store after a test run.
Test column-level resolution on representative transformations (joins, aggregates, CASE) for correct mappings.
Validate idempotency by re-emitting the same run id and confirming no duplicate nodes/edges.

commonMistakes.whyItHappens: It seems quick to write a wiki page or diagram, and automated capture feels like extra work.
commonMistakes.impact: Documentation goes stale immediately as pipelines evolve, so impact analysis and root-cause traces are wrong or missing.
commonMistakes.correctApproach: Automate lineage capture with OpenLineage integrations or native catalog lineage so the graph reflects what actually runs.

commonMistakes.mistake: Settling for table-level lineage when column-level is needed.
commonMistakes.whyItHappens: Table-level is easier to capture and visualize, and the gap isn't obvious until a column-specific question arises.
commonMistakes.impact: Can't trace where a specific (e.g., PII) column flows or precisely scope a column change, leading to over-broad or missed impact.
commonMistakes.correctApproach: Capture column-level lineage (via SQL parsing or a catalog that supports it) for compliance and precise impact analysis.

commonMistakes.mistake: Letting lineage emission block or break the pipeline.
commonMistakes.whyItHappens: Emitting events synchronously inline is the simplest implementation.
commonMistakes.impact: A slow or down metadata store adds latency to or fails the actual data pipeline — lineage becomes a liability.
commonMistakes.correctApproach: Emit asynchronously and idempotently with buffering/retries so lineage capture never affects pipeline reliability.

commonMistakes.whyItHappens: Different integrations or teams name the same physical table differently (aliases, paths, case).
commonMistakes.impact: The lineage graph fragments — the same dataset appears as multiple nodes, breaking upstream/downstream traversal.
commonMistakes.correctApproach: Standardize fully-qualified namespace+name conventions so every emitter references shared datasets identically.

comparisonSection.explanation: Table-level shows which datasets feed which — cheap, simple, good for high-level dependency maps. Column-level maps each output column to its source columns — richer and harder to compute, but required for PII tracing and minimal-blast-radius impact analysis.

Static parsing derives intended dependencies from code without execution (great for pre-deploy impact analysis) but can miss dynamic behavior. Runtime emission captures what actually ran, with timing and failures, ideal for operational observability and audit.

OpenLineage is a tool-agnostic open standard with Marquez as the reference store, ideal for heterogeneous stacks. Unity Catalog auto-captures table and column lineage natively within Databricks — lower effort but scoped to that platform; many orgs bridge both.

Lineage is the dependency graph (provenance/impact/root cause) of how data flows. A catalog organizes and describes/searches datasets. Modern catalogs embed lineage, but they are distinct capabilities — discovery vs traceability.

beginnerQuestions.question: What is data lineage and what questions does it answer?
beginnerQuestions.answer: Data lineage is the end-to-end tracking of data's origin, movement, and transformations. It answers where data came from (provenance), what transformations it underwent, and what downstream artifacts depend on it (impact), supporting root-cause debugging and compliance.
beginnerQuestions.explanation: Cover provenance (upstream), impact (downstream), and the practical uses: debugging, impact analysis, audit.

beginnerQuestions.question: What is the difference between table-level and column-level lineage?
beginnerQuestions.answer: Table-level lineage tracks which datasets feed which (producer-consumer between whole tables). Column-level lineage maps each output column to the specific source columns and functions that derive it, enabling precise impact analysis and PII tracing.
beginnerQuestions.explanation: Emphasize column-level is finer-grained and needed for compliance and minimal-blast-radius change analysis.

intermediateQuestions.question: How is lineage captured automatically, and what is OpenLineage?
intermediateQuestions.answer: Lineage is captured by parsing transformation SQL/query plans (static) or by emitting runtime events from jobs as they run. OpenLineage is an open standard (Linux Foundation) defining a model and API for emitting lineage events — runs, jobs, datasets, and extensible facets (schema, columnLineage) — across tools like Airflow, Spark, and dbt, with Marquez as the reference metadata store.
intermediateQuestions.explanation: Distinguish static vs runtime capture and name OpenLineage's run/job/dataset/facet model and Marquez.

intermediateQuestions.question: How would you use lineage for impact analysis before changing a column?
intermediateQuestions.answer: Query downstream (out-edge) lineage starting from the dataset/column to enumerate every job, table, dashboard, and model that depends on it. With column-level lineage you can scope precisely to consumers of that column, then notify owners and plan changes to avoid breakage.
intermediateQuestions.explanation: Show the downstream traversal and that column-level lineage narrows the true blast radius.

advancedQuestions.question: How would you design lineage capture so it never impacts pipeline reliability or performance at scale?
advancedQuestions.answer: Decouple emission from execution: integrations emit lineage events asynchronously to a queue, not inline. Make ingestion idempotent by run id so retries don't double-count. Buffer events so a metadata-store outage queues rather than loses or blocks. Resolve column-level lineage incrementally per run, and degrade to table-level if parsing fails. Treat lineage coverage as an SLI and monitor ingestion lag.
advancedQuestions.explanation: Key themes: async + idempotent + buffered emission, graceful degradation, and monitoring coverage as an SLI.

advancedQuestions.question: What are the challenges of accurate column-level lineage, and how do you handle them?
advancedQuestions.answer: Challenges include SELECT * obscuring mappings, UDFs and dynamic SQL the parser can't introspect, complex CASE/aggregation/window expressions, and cross-engine differences. Mitigations: forbid SELECT * in transformations, prefer engines/catalogs with native plan-based column lineage (e.g., Unity Catalog reading the logical plan), document unresolved derivations explicitly, and fall back to table-level where column resolution is impossible.
advancedQuestions.explanation: Demonstrate awareness that column-level lineage is often incomplete and the practical ways to maximize and bound its accuracy.

scenarioBasedQuestions.scenario: A compliance team needs to prove exactly where customer PII (email, SSN) flows across your platform and confirm it isn't leaking into a public-facing dashboard. How do you use lineage to answer this?
scenarioBasedQuestions.thinkingProcess: This is a column-level, downstream-traversal problem. Identify the PII source columns, then traverse column-level lineage downstream to enumerate every derived column and dataset, checking whether any path reaches the public dashboard. Table-level alone is insufficient because it can't tell whether the specific PII columns propagate.
scenarioBasedQuestions.expectedAnswer: Use column-level lineage to start from source PII columns (e.g., customers.email, customers.ssn) and traverse downstream out-edges to find every column/dataset derived from them. Verify whether any path reaches the public dashboard's columns; if so, that's the leak path. Provide the traced paths as audit evidence and use the same lineage to scope remediation (mask/remove the offending derivation). This requires column-level (not just table-level) lineage and is exactly the kind of compliance proof regulations like GDPR demand.

systemDesignQuestions.problemStatement: Design an end-to-end data lineage system for a heterogeneous platform (Airflow + Spark + dbt + a warehouse + BI/ML) that supports impact analysis, root-cause debugging, and compliance, at the scale of thousands of datasets and runs per day.
systemDesignQuestions.designApproach: Standardize on OpenLineage: instrument Airflow, Spark, and dbt with OpenLineage integrations that emit run events (inputs/outputs + schema + columnLineage facets) asynchronously to a queue. Ingest into a metadata store/catalog (Marquez or DataHub, or bridge to Unity Catalog) that materializes a versioned DAG with run history and exposes search/traversal APIs and a UI. Add a column-level resolver (or rely on native plan-based lineage). Integrate data-quality facets for observability.
systemDesignQuestions.tradeOffs: Open standard (OpenLineage) gives tool-agnostic coverage but requires instrumenting each tool; platform-native lineage (Unity Catalog) is lower-effort but scoped. Column-level lineage adds value but is costlier and can be incomplete. Asynchronous emission protects pipeline reliability at the cost of slight lineage lag. Many orgs bridge open + native lineage.
systemDesignQuestions.scalingStrategy: Buffer/queue events for high-throughput idempotent ingestion keyed by run id; version datasets and TTL old runs; index upstream/downstream closures for fast impact queries; bound traversal depth; resolve column lineage incrementally per run; monitor lineage coverage and ingestion lag as SLIs; run the store as an HA service with a durable, replicated backing database.

keyTakeaways: Data lineage is the end-to-end, queryable record of where data came from, how it was transformed, and what depends on it, powering provenance, impact analysis, root-cause debugging, and compliance.

It comes in granularities: table-level (which datasets feed which) is simpler, while column-level (which source columns derive each target column) is essential for PII tracing and precise impact analysis.

Lineage is captured statically by parsing SQL/code or at runtime by emitting events — the OpenLineage standard (with Marquez) and platform-native catalogs like Unity Catalog automate this across heterogeneous stacks.
Production lineage must be automated, consistently named, captured asynchronously and idempotently so it never breaks pipelines, and monitored as an SLI to avoid impact-analysis blind spots.
